description: Create an event in the signed-in account from GPX files or links: a cycling ride, tour or race (Windline) or a run or running race (RunFast). Pass every GPX the user gave as files: several files make a multi-day tour by themselves (never ask for the type when it's obvious), ordered by the numbers in their names (1, 01, "day-2", "Stage 3"), else by the map (each day starts where the last ended); day names, km, climbing and a suggested name come from the files, and the days follow one another from start, at the same time, skipping rest_days. The first call (without confirm) only reads the files and returns the plan: show the user that summary (days, order, dates, km, private or for a group) in one message and get one yes, then call again with the same files and confirm: true. visibility: private is just for them (Windline My Rides with its own private link, or a RunFast private run: never published, never on a page); shared is for a group, published later with publish_event. A personal ride or run someone is planning for themselves is private. If the signed-in person runs any club or organiser page (list_my_events lists them) and hasn't said who it's for, ask one short question first: is this a private ride or run for you, or a group ride or run for <club name>? Then use post_club_ride for the club, or create_event with visibility private for themselves. Tour notes for riders the organiser pasted or attached (text, markdown, or a document's text) go in notes, up to 10,000 characters (Windline tours, beta). A route can also come from another app's tool as its points or an encoded polyline (for example a route or activity map from a fitness app): pass it as polyline or points. Never ask the user to export a GPX if you already have the route's points.

club.description: RunFast: the club address (one they manage).

confirm.description: With files: true only after the user said yes to the plan this tool returned.

days.description: One per day (a ride or a run: one). Or give url with a Ride with GPS collection and starts.

gpx.description: The GPX file's text (up to 5 MB): if the user pasted it, or attached a file you can read yourself (for example with code).

points.description: The route as its points: [[lat, lon], …], with elevation in metres as a third number if known. Up to 50,000. Use it for points another app's tool gave, or that you read from an attached file (GPX, FIT, TCX) with code.

polyline.description: The route as an encoded polyline (Google's format, precision 5 or 6), as another app's tool gives it (a route's or an activity's map).

start.description: Local start, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" in the route's own time zone.

url.description: A link to the route: a Ride with GPS route, ride or collection (a collection gives one day per route), or any public link to a GPX file. Not Strava.

description.description: What the event is, for its public page.

files.description: Every GPX the user attached or linked, in the order they came: one per day of a tour, one for a ride or run.

items.description: A GPX file (its text, or a link to it) or a route's polyline or points, and its name (the name helps order the days).

download_url.description: ChatGPT: the attached file's download link.

points.description: The day as its points, [[lat, lon], …].

polyline.description: The day as an encoded polyline (another app's route or activity map).

url.description: A link to the GPX or route (Ride with GPS; not Strava).

gpx_file.description: The GPX or route file the user attached (ChatGPT passes it here).

file_name.description: Its name, if known (the route's name; never an event's).

gpx_files.description: Several GPX or route files the user attached (ChatGPT passes them here): one per day of a tour, ordered by the numbers in their names, else by the map.

items.description: One attached GPX or route file.

file_name.description: Its name, if known (the route's name; never an event's).

name.description: The event's name; with files, left out to use the suggested one.

notes.description: Tours: the organiser's notes for riders (what to pack, meeting points), as they pasted or attached them, markdown, up to 10,000 characters. RunFast: a short note (600 characters).

pace.description: Riding km/h, or running seconds per km.

page.description: Windline: the club or organiser page address to show it on (one they run).

place.description: RunFast: where it starts, in words.

points.description: The route as its points: [[lat, lon], …], with elevation in metres as a third number if known. Up to 50,000. Use it for points another app's tool gave, or that you read from an attached file (GPX, FIT, TCX) with code.

polyline.description: The route as an encoded polyline (Google's format, precision 5 or 6), as another app's tool gives it (a route's or an activity's map). One route: a ride, a run or a one-day race (with start).

race.description: RunFast: a race (once, with a gun time) rather than a run.

rest_days.description: With files: dates with no riding, "YYYY-MM-DD", only if the user named rest days.

start.description: With files: day 1's local start, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM" (the same time every day unless starts says otherwise). Ask if they didn't say.

starts.description: Each day's own local start, "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", when they differ (with url or files).

type.description: ride, tour or race on Windline (cycling); run on RunFast (a running race: type run with race: true). Leave it out when it's obvious: several files make a tour, one file a ride (or a run on a RunFast account).

tz.description: IANA time zone; else worked out from where the route starts.

url.description: A Ride with GPS collection for a multi-day tour (one day per route), used with starts.

visibility.description: private: just for them (My Rides; a private run). shared: for a group, published later. Ask if they run a club and didn't say.

weekly.description: A weekly ride or run: { days: [0-6, Sunday is 0], time: "HH:MM" }.
